title: Monsoon and Horizon
premise: When the Kestrel River spits out a salvage chest bearing the seal of Vhaloria — a drowned nation erased from every map forty years ago — blacklisted mountain guide Jonah Amberdale recognizes the crest from his grandfather's forbidden letters. The chest is a claim marker: whoever reaches the sunken archive beneath Glacier Meridian before calving season can prove Vhaloria's last government legally deeded its treasury to its refugees, including Jonah's family. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet through six tides of narrowing ice corridors, Jonah discovers his grandfather helped sink the nation deliberately to hide evidence of a massacre. In the flooded archive, Jonah must choose between vindicating his bloodline and exposing it; he publishes everything, guilty and innocent alike, letting justice fall outside any court's reach. The glacier closes behind him as he walks out carrying nothing but the truth.
about_author: Ada Whitlock is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent nine seasons in high-latitude field camps before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that keep better records than governments.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Blacklisted and guiding illegal crossings to survive, Jonah pulls a sealed chest from the Kestrel after a flood. Inside: a wax-stamped claim deed naming his grandfather. Emotional beat: wary curiosity hardening into dread when he realizes the seal belongs to a country that officially never existed.

chapters.title: The Letters Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with flashback interludes. He rereads his grandfather's coded letters and deciphers coordinates beneath Glacier Meridian. A salvage broker's men arrive asking about 'river debris.' Emotional beat: grief for the grandfather he resented, tangled with the first thrill of purpose in years.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He recruits his estranged former partner, river pilot Sefa Okonkwo, calculating that only six navigable tides remain before ice chokepoints close. The salvage fleet departs the same night. Emotional beat: brittle reconciliation built on mutual distrust and shared history.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Dawn
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Outmaneuvered at the first narrows, they hide in a sea cave while the fleet's sonar drones sweep past. Jonah admits the blacklist was earned protecting a client he should have abandoned. Emotional beat: shame confessed, partially absolved by Sefa's dry forgiveness.

chapters.title: Country of Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In an abandoned refugee waystation, murals depict Vhaloria's final days — and name Jonah's grandfather as Minister of Interior. The massacre he'd suspected becomes personal. Emotional beat: inheritance curdling into horror; the quest stops being about treasure.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Captured briefly by the fleet, Sefa learns the broker is Vhalorian-descended too, seeking to destroy the archive and keep the erasure permanent. She escapes with a stolen tide chart. Emotional beat: fury transformed into resolve; the race becomes a moral one.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A storm costs them the fifth tide entirely; Sefa nearly drowns holding the chart above water. They argue about turning back. Emotional beat: despair, then quiet commitment — Sefa chooses to stay not for justice but for Jonah.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, claustrophobic and hushed. On the sixth tide they dive into the flooded vault and find the full record: the grandfather ordered the scuttling to bury proof of the massacre he failed to prevent. Emotional beat: devastating clarity — the man was both perpetrator and penitent.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The fleet arrives as the glacier begins to calve; the broker offers Jonah silence in exchange for the originals. He refuses, transmits copies to refugee networks worldwide, and the collapse destroys the vault and nearly them both. Emotional beat: climax — defiance at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: Monsoon and Horizon
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Weeks later, the truth spreads beyond any court's power to contain; some refugees mourn, some rage, all finally know. Jonah and Sefa guide a memorial crossing to where the nation now lies under open water. Emotional beat: peace without absolution — memory inherited honestly at last.
